newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian analysts welcome Clinton victory.
newsitem.headline: Indian analysts welcome Clinton victory.

text.p: Political analysts in India welcomed Bill Clinton's U.S. re-election victory on Wednesday and said they hoped his new administration would take a fresh perspective on bilateral relations.
"I consider Clinton's re-election augurs well for good relations between the two countries," said V.A. Pai Panandikar, director of the independent Centre for Policy Research.

Analysts said economic ties between the two countries, which swiftly improved after India introduced a market liberalisation programme in 1991 after decades of socialist controls, would continue to grow.

"We have our problems with the U.S., much of which arose during the run-up to the (U.S.) election. The new administration will get more time to look into that," said Rasheed Talib, an independent political analyst.

India and the United States have differed mainly on nuclear policy and trade issues in the World Trade Organisation. India opposed the global nuclear test ban treaty and blocked its adoption in Geneva in August.
Talib hoped Clinton's new administration would give more time to and have fresh perspectives on some of these issues.
"There might be a different perspective by the new administration, depending on the new set of officers," he said.

Analysts said political upheavel in neighbouring Pakistan, following the dismissal of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's government, might help the United States to view India in a different perspective.
"The way Pakistan has gone, we (India) might be the only beacon of democracy in the region. I hope there is a better appreciation of the difficulties of democracy in the region," Talib said.
"Therefore, they would not want to push us further on issues," he added.
